observations.title: East Middle School: refuge areas and exposure
observations.locator: Section 3.3.2.1, printed page 210 (PDF page 274); Figure 3-123, printed page 211 (PDF page 275).
observations.account: NIST reports minor roof covering damage in six designated refuge areas despite collapse of the gymnasium and auditorium. It describes protective construction features and lower estimated winds over much of the refuge portion as the likely explanation for their performance.
observations.limits: The school was unoccupied. This is building performance evidence, not an observed occupant survival result. NIST lacked direct information on how the areas were selected, and the drawings did not specify tornado design. Estimated winds are not direct measurements.

observations.title: Joplin High School: surviving areas, unknown use
observations.locator: Section 3.3.2.2, printed pages 210 and 213 (PDF pages 274 and 277); Figure 3-124, printed page 212 (PDF page 276).
observations.account: NIST found no structural damage in designated refuge areas despite major damage elsewhere in the school. It describes interior protected locations as the best available refuge, rather than engineered tornado shelters.
observations.limits: NIST had only partial drawings and did not know the selection process, building occupancy or whether anyone sheltered there. No reported injuries does not establish successful occupied sheltering. The report is historical evidence, not current safety or building design advice.

observations.title: When the first siren stopped
observations.locator: Section 2b, Finding 2a, printed page 5 (PDF page 11). Section 2a methodology and footnote 4, printed page 4 (PDF page 10). Survival limits on printed page 9 (PDF page 15).
observations.account: The July 2011 NWS assessment describes Joplin's sirens sounding in one three-minute burst and then stopping. Several interviewees interpreted that silence as the threat being over. The report distinguishes the alert from the information people needed to understand the nature and magnitude of the danger.
observations.limits: The warning-response section uses 54 residents' perspectives from 63 interviews, with nine excluded. NWS describes a limited local case study, not a population rate. The report does not establish how many people who died failed to shelter or whether a different response would have changed survival. This is historical policy and reported interpretation, not current siren guidance or an individual response clock.

observations.title: The first siren and a different warned storm
observations.locator: Section 3, Storm-Based Warnings and Local Warning Dissemination Systems, printed page 13 (PDF page 19), paragraphs preceding the single interview example. Methods and dissemination context: printed pages 11 to 12 (PDF pages 17 to 18).
observations.account: The July 2011 NWS assessment attributes the 5:11 p.m. CDT siren activation primarily to funnel-cloud reports west of Joplin. It distinguishes those reports from warning 30, issued two minutes earlier for a different storm affecting western Jasper County and northeastern Joplin. Some interviewees combined the siren with the northern warning details and thought the threat was to the north.
observations.limits: This is the assessment's attributed explanation of the Emergency Manager's decision and selected interviews. It is not an independently reconstructed alert chain, a population estimate or a mortality explanation. The report's historical clock labels supply no individual reception time or video alignment. Current siren policy was not investigated.

media.title: The West Tower remained standing
media.locator: Figure 3-9, north side of the West Tower, printed page 96 (PDF page 160).
